Title: Diagnosis of test `testAddNonComparable`

Details:
- The test `testAddNonComparable` checks the behavior of the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method when adding a non-comparable object.
- The failure occurs because the test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown when `f.addValue(new Object())` is called.
- Examining the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method:
  - It is deprecated and delegates to `addValue(Comparable<?>)` by casting the input object to `Comparable<?>`.
- Examining the `Frequency.addValue(Comparable<?>)` method:
  - It tries to insert the value into a frequency table (likely a TreeMap).
  - If the input is an instance of `Integer`, it is converted to a `Long`.
  - When `freqTable.get(obj)` is called, it attempts a lookup.
  - If a `ClassCastException` is caught (which happens if the object is not comparable to existing keys in the TreeMap), it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."
- The test expects this `IllegalArgumentException`, confirming the code behaves as expected for non-comparable values.
- If the test failed, possible reasons could be:
  - The exception was not thrown (i.e., `ClassCastException` was not caught/handled).
  - A different exception or no exception was thrown.
  - The cast in `addValue(Object)` may not actually be enforcing Comparable causing a `ClassCastException` at the caller level or a ClassCastException instead of `IllegalArgumentException`.
  
In summary, the bug likely relates to the handling and type casting in `addValue(Object)` or the exception handling in `addValue(Comparable<?>)` when adding an object that does not implement Comparable.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testAddNonComparable`

Details:
- The `freqTable` field is a `TreeMap`.
- `TreeMap` in Java requires keys to be mutually comparable, otherwise it will throw a `ClassCastException` during insertion or lookup.
- The `Frequency` constructor initializes `freqTable` as a plain `TreeMap`.
- The `Frequency.addValue(Object v)` method is deprecated; it casts the value to `Comparable<?>` and calls `addValue(Comparable<?>)`.
- The `addValue(Comparable<?>)` method attempts to insert the Comparable object into `freqTable`.
- If the object is not compatible with existing keys, a `ClassCastException` thrown by `TreeMap.get` or `put` is caught and wrapped into an `IllegalArgumentException`.
- The test calls `f.addValue(new Object())` with a raw `Object` that does not implement `Comparable`.
- This cast to `Comparable<?>` in `addValue(Object v)` does not cause a compile-time or runtime exception because the cast is unchecked.
- When `addValue(Comparable<?>)` is called with a non-Comparable object, it leads to a `ClassCastException` when the TreeMap tries to compare the new key with existing keys.
- The `ClassCastException` should be caught and an `IllegalArgumentException` thrown.
- The test expects the `IllegalArgumentException`.
  
If the test fails, it must be that the `ClassCastException` is not being thrown or caught properly, or the input value does not cause a `ClassCastException`. Another possibility is the map is empty so no comparison is done, thus no exception thrown. Because if the map is empty, `freqTable.get(obj)` or `freqTable.put(obj, something)` won't do any comparisons causing no exceptions.

The bug likely occurs because the first insertion into an empty `TreeMap` with a non-comparable object does not cause any exception, and the test expects an exception regardless. Previously adding a non-comparable object was "OK" when the map was empty, but the test expects it to fail in all cases.

Hence the bug is caused by the test assuming `addValue` throws exception even when the map is empty and no comparison can happen. This is a behavior change or discrepancy.

Summary:
- The test fails because adding a new non-comparable value to an empty frequency map does not throw `IllegalArgumentException` since no comparison is made.
- `ClassCastException` will only happen when the map already has comparable type keys and a new incompatible key is added.
- Thus the test's expectation is incorrect, or the code needs to check comparability earlier.

Suggested fix locations to handle this case explicitly or update the test's expectations.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Comparable<?>)
